SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Heating until a solid melts

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Nitrogen gas only

3. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Producers
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Decomposers only

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

9. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Burning crop residue every week

10. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Milk souring

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.

12. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

2. C — Glucose and oxygen

3. B — Producers

4. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

5. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.

6. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

8. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

9. B — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

10. A — Ice melting to water

11. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

12. A — 100 °C

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Levers as simple machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Slopes as simple machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Invertebrates; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Change of State; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
